clue.text: Indexed material for art exhibition…

parts.note: read 'Indexed' as applied with the index finger: a substance smeared on by hand to make a picture for display

explanation.surface: Some catalogued material is being prepared for a gallery show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indexed' suggests a catalogue or reference book; here it means put on with the index finger, the way children make pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a paint children apply with their digits instead of brushes, hence material put on by the index.

clue.text: Divine appropriate to English diocese

parts.note: something appropriate to an occasion is for it
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A clergyman is well suited to an English church district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like a noun meaning a clergyman, but it is a verb meaning to predict.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine the future is to predict or anticipate it.

clue.text: Glamorgan town rebuilt from the ruins of Athens? Not quite!

indicators.note: something rebuilt from ruins is reassembled in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered
not quite the whole word, so the final letter of Athens is cut off

explanation.surface: A Welsh town claims to have been reconstructed from Greek ruins, which is not exactly true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter of ATHENS to leave ATHEN, which 'rebuilt from the ruins of' rearranges. Glamorgan is a historic county in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an industrial town near Swansea in the historic Welsh county of Glamorgan.

clue.text: Article in which I lead, or it is altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor claims that their piece is changed when they take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges I LEAD OR IT; 'in which' and 'is' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article expressing its own opinion is a leader, written by the editor's team.

clue.text: This head, with accent, could be 16

definitions.meaning: an old word for the top of the head
with accents added it becomes a savoury meat paste, which could be served as the Italian starter at 16 Down

explanation.surface: A head with a certain accent might be served as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' is a link word. With a circumflex and acute accent the word becomes the French meat spread, which could be eaten as an antipasto (16 Down).
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for the crown of the head, and with accents it names a meat spread eaten as a starter.

clue.text: Where striker stands-and what he is out for

definitions.meaning: the batter facing in cricket stands inside the marked line at the wicket
he is out to get more runs, a growth in the score

explanation.surface: A batsman at the crease and what he is hoping to achieve.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the striker is the batsman facing the bowler, standing in the crease, the line marked in front of the stumps; 'out for' means seeking, not dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word says where a cricket batsman stands; whole, it means growth, which is what he seeks in his score.

clue.text: Refuse lago's purse

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun means rubbish
in Othello, Iago says that whoever steals his purse steals rubbish

explanation.surface: A villain declines to hand over his wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun for rubbish. In Shakespeare's Othello, Iago says 'Who steals my purse steals trash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is worthless waste, and Shakespeare's villain dismisses his own purse with that very word.

clue.text: Freud as yearly record-keeper, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by how it sounds when said

parts.note: an annalist keeps annals, records year by year

explanation.surface: Freud is described as someone who kept an annual diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' means the answer sounds like ANNALIST, a writer of annals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud founded psychoanalysis and is the archetypal psychoanalyst, or shrink.

clue.text: For space between electrodes, set offblank

parts.note: to spark something is to set it off or trigger it
a blank is a gap or empty space

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a blank between electrodes in a technical diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word; the definition is a technical term for the gap across which a spark jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: In electrical engineering, the gap between two electrodes across which a discharge jumps bears this name.

clue.text: … articles I ordered to be true to life

indicators.note: the letters of the words 'articles I' are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Some items have been arranged so as to look lifelike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges ARTICLES I; 'to be' links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifelike in its portrayal is realistic, faithfully depicting how things are.

clue.text: Star mark in examination

definitions.meaning: the brightest star of a constellation is given the first Greek letter as its label
a top grade, an A, can be called by the first Greek letter

explanation.surface: A top performer earns a stellar grade in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter labels a constellation's brightest star and also serves as a top exam grade, the equivalent of an A.

clue.text: Followers of harrow, say

parts.note: the word that comes after the name Harrow in the full title of the famous English boarding institution, which is an example of the type

explanation.surface: Farm workers trail behind a harrow across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English private boarding establishment; the word following its name in its full title, Harrow ___, is the answer, and the sense is a teaching institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrow is an instance of a place of education, and in its full name the word comes right after Harrow.

clue.text: Sluggishness greatly affected by intake of hydrogen

indicators.note: an intake of something means it is taken in, so the hydrogen symbol goes inside the rearranged letters
affected here means disturbed or altered, so the letters of 'greatly' are rearranged

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Lethargy is said to be strongly influenced by breathing in a certain gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges the letters of 'greatly', and 'intake of' means the hydrogen symbol is taken in by that new arrangement; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a state of torpor and sluggishness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: Cake that goes like lightning in France…

definitions.meaning: a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate
the French word for a lightning flash

explanation.surface: A pastry disappears in a flash on the other side of the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that goes like' is linking: the cake's French name literally means a flash of lightning, perhaps because it is eaten so fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream-filled choux pastry takes its name from the French word for a lightning flash.

clue.text: Abundance of ropes for making things fast

definitions.meaning: plenty, a large quantity, as in cream in great quantities
cords used to tie things securely

explanation.surface: A sailor has plenty of rope for securing the cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the two definitions; 'fast' means secure, not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means great quantities and also the cords used to tie things down securely.

clue.text: … whereas this delicacy of theirs went slowly

definitions.text: whereas this delicacy of theirs went slowly

parts.words: whereas this delicacy of theirs went slowly
parts.note: continuing the previous clue's French theme: a French dish known for crawling at a snail's pace, unlike the pastry that went like lightning

explanation.surface: In contrast to the quick French cake, this French treat moved at a crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to 13 Across: 'theirs' means the French, and the delicacy that goes slowly is the snail, served in garlic butter.
explanation.definitionFit: This French delicacy is the edible snail, the creature proverbial for moving slowly.

clue.text: Not at Pisa, perhaps, this course? On the contrary!

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish not served in Pisa, maybe; but in fact it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NOT AT PISA. 'On the contrary!' teases: this Italian starter would indeed be found in Pisa.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian starter course of cold meats and vegetables comes before the pasta.

clue.text: The boxer not fancied could be grounded

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxing outsider might end up knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges GROUNDED; the definition plays on the boxer as a dog breed too.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor not expected to win is the outsider in a contest.

clue.text: Vulgar streak at end of court

parts.note: base means low, coarse or vulgar
a streak is a line or stripe

explanation.surface: A tennis player displays a coarse temperament at the back of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word; in tennis the line marking each end of the court has this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the boundary at each end of the playing area is the line players serve from.

clue.text: Slow bird with bright body in rudimentary flower

indicators.note: in tells us the bright body goes inside the rudimentary flower

parts.note: a bud is an undeveloped flower
a star is a bright heavenly body

explanation.surface: A sluggish bird with a vivid body sits in an undeveloped bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'in' places the bright body inside the bud, splitting it after its second letter. 'Slow' fits the bird's heavy, stately gait.
explanation.definitionFit: This large heavy ground bird of open plains walks steadily and is a slow flier.

clue.text: Promotion for a riser

parts.note: a rise in rank for someone climbing the ladder, playing on a riser as the vertical part of a stair

explanation.surface: Someone who gets up early earns advancement at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A riser is both someone who rises and the upright part of a staircase step, so going higher one stair also describes a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving to a higher position at work is an upward move, like climbing one stair.

clue.text: Developer of jetty unit inside

indicators.note: inside places the unit within the jetty

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A property developer has a single jetty block inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word; 'inside' puts the unit within the jetty word, after its second letter. 'Developer' suggests property, but means a trailblazer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who develops something new is a trailblazer or innovator, a first settler of fresh ground.

clue.text: Eruption to be treated by a house doctor?

definitions.meaning: a painful skin rash caused by the virus behind chickenpox

definitions.text: to be treated by a house doctor?
definitions.meaning: roof tiles of wood, which a builder treating a house would repair

explanation.surface: A rash needs to be seen by a hospital's resident physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house doctor' suggests a resident hospital physician, but read it as someone who mends houses: the roof tiles share the name of the rash.
explanation.definitionFit: The viral skin eruption and wooden roof tiles share one name, so both a doctor and a roofer deal with them.

clue.text: The colour for putting on

definitions.meaning: the area of short grass in golf where players putt

explanation.surface: A colour is chosen to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting on' suggests dressing, but means golfers putting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the colour of grass and also the smooth golf area around the hole where players putt.

clue.text: Rocket that gets ahead on oxygen

parts.note: read as 'a head': A plus poll, an old word for the head
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A rocket gets in front by burning oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ahead' splits into 'a head', and POLL is the head (as in a poll tax, levied per head); 'that gets' and 'on' link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The American programme that sent astronauts to the Moon used rockets bearing this name.

clue.text: The first from Leyton Orient is the minutest

indicators.note: the first from points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: The first player from a London football club is the smallest.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club, but here Orient means the East; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutest means smallest, the superlative of tiny.

clue.text: Bookworm pulls up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tows means pulls

explanation.surface: A studious reader hauls something upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TOWS, which reads upward in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-working student who studies obsessively is a grind or bookworm.

clue.text: Some fear guesswork and show by reasoning

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people distrust speculation and prefer to prove things logically.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a case through reasoning is to contend or demonstrate by logic.

clue.text: Towards the pit for the cast

definitions.text: Towards the pit for the cast

parts.words: Towards the pit for the cast
parts.note: the direction actors move when heading to the front of the stage, nearest the orchestra pit

explanation.surface: Miners are being sent down towards the coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pit' suggests a mine but means the orchestra pit in front of a theatre stage; actors moving towards the audience go this way.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, moving towards the front of the stage, nearest the audience and orchestra pit, has this name.

clue.text: Hotel worker on late shift has dark ale

parts.note: the dark is nighttime
porter is a dark brown beer

explanation.surface: A hotel employee working late enjoys a dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word; porter is a dark beer once drunk by London market porters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel employee who staffs the front desk through the small hours is this kind of attendant.
